items.text: Quasi-compact morphisms
Stable under base change: $S,S'$ affine, $X=\bigcup_{\text{finite}}U_i$ with $U_i$ affine $\Rightarrow$ $X'=\bigcup X_i'$, $X_i'=X_i\times_S S'$ affine.
Stable under composition.
$G$ quasi-separated (diagonal quasi-compact), $G\circ F$ quasi-compact $\Rightarrow$ $F$ quasi-compact.
Finite type, finite presentation
$f\colon X\to S$ of finite type: quasi-compact, and for $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ affine, $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}$ affine, $B$ is an $A$-algebra of finite type.
Finite type = quasi-compact + locally of finite type (all such $B$ of finite type over $A$).
Locally of finite presentation: same with $B$ of finite presentation over $A$; both notions are local on $X$.
X=\operatorname{Spec}B,\ S=\operatorname{Spec}A:\quad\text{loc. of finite type}\iff B\ \text{of finite type over }A;\qquad\text{loc. of finite presentation}\iff B\ \text{of finite presentation}
$S$ locally noetherian: finite type $=$ finite presentation.
All these classes are stable under base change and composition.
Immersions
Open immersion: homeomorphism onto an open subset of $Y$, with $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y|_X$. A monomorphism; stable under base change and composition.
Closed immersions
First definition: $Y=\bigcup Y_i$ affine; $X_i=f^{-1}(Y_i)$ affine and $A_i\to B_i$ surjective.
Intrinsic definition: $f$ a homeomorphism of $X$ onto a closed subset of $Y$, and
\mathcal O_Y\longrightarrow f_*\mathcal O_X\ \text{surjective, kernel }\mathcal J,\qquad f_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J
The kernel $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent (needs $f_*\mathcal O_X$ quasi-coherent).
A closed immersion is a monomorphism: closed subschemes of $Y$ $\leftrightarrow$ quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_Y$.
\mathcal J\longmapsto V(\mathcal J)=\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J,\ \mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J\bigr)

X=V(\mathcal J)=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J):\qquad X'=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal O_{Y'}\bigr)=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathcal O_{Y'}/\mathcal J\mathcal O_{Y'}\bigr)
Closed immersions are stable under base change.
\mathcal J\subset\mathcal K\subset\mathcal O_Y\ \leftrightarrow\ \mathcal K/\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_X;\qquad \mathcal K\ \text{q.c.}\iff\mathcal K/\mathcal J\ \text{q.c.}
Hence transitivity: closed in closed is closed.
Summary of classes of morphisms
Local below: affine, quasi-compact, finite type. Local above and below: locally of finite type, locally of finite presentation.
Open subschemes $\leftrightarrow$ open subsets; closed subschemes $\leftrightarrow$ quasi-coherent ideals, order-reversing.

X_1\times_Y X_2=X_1\cap X_2:\qquad V(\mathcal J_1)\cap V(\mathcal J_2)=V(\mathcal J_1+\mathcal J_2),\quad \mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J_2=\mathcal O_Y/(\mathcal J_1+\mathcal J_2)
Immersions
Immersion: $f=f'\circ f_c$, $f_c$ a closed immersion, $f'$ an open immersion.
X\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }V(\mathcal J)\hookrightarrow U\subset Y,\qquad \mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_U\ \text{quasi-coherent}
$X$ locally closed in $Y$; the largest $U$ is the complement of $\overline X\setminus X$.
f\ \text{homeomorphism onto a locally closed subset},\qquad f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X\ \text{surjective}
Equivalently: every $y\in f(X)$ has an open (affine) neighborhood $V$ with $X|_V\to V$ a closed immersion.
His « immersion » is the differential geometers' « embedding ».
Immersions are stable under base change and composition.
Diagonal morphisms are immersions
\Delta\colon X\to X\times_S X\ \text{is an immersion}\iff\text{every section }g\colon S\to X\ \text{is an immersion}
Proof: local on $S$, so $S$ affine; $f$ the structure morphism, $g$ a section; take an affine open $U\ni g(s)$ of $X$ and look at $g^{-1}(U)$.
